title: The Lantern Keeper's Daughter
author: Mara Bell
description: A daughter returns to a remote island to close her father's lighthouse and finds a final season of letters, storms, and unfinished promises.

title: A Memory of Europa
author: Iris Vale
description: A mission historian reconstructs the last day of a lost expedition from fragments that keep changing whenever they are read.

title: The River Road Atlas
author: Eli Winters
description: A retired guide and a young mapmaker follow a river from its first spring to the sea, finding a different kind of courage at every bend.

title: How to Hold a Morning
author: Nina March
description: Short poems for beginnings, unfinished cups of tea, early trains, and the first brave hour of a difficult day.

title: The Missing Hour
author: Owen Hart
description: Every clock in a small hotel loses the same sixty minutes. A new guest is the only person who remembers what happened inside the missing hour.

title: Cities by Candlelight
author: Sana Cole
description: A collection of night walks through six cities, told through food stalls, quiet museums, local legends, and the people who keep streets alive after dark.

title: Rest as a Practice
author: Rowan Pierce
description: A practical guide to recovering attention, setting kinder boundaries, and treating rest as a skill rather than a reward.

title: The Small Business Field Guide
author: Avery Cole
description: A clear, practical guide to validating an idea, finding first customers, pricing honestly, and building a business that can last.

title: Clearer Meetings
author: Dara Kim
description: Simple systems for making meetings shorter, decisions clearer, and collaboration more useful for the people doing the actual work.

title: The Honest Brand
author: Clara West
description: How small teams can build trust through useful promises, consistent language, and products that do what they say on the label.

title: Work That Works
author: Priya Sen
description: A humane operating guide for independent teams covering priorities, feedback, documentation, and the habits that protect deep work.

title: The Friendly Machine
author: Theo March
description: A non-technical introduction to thinking clearly about AI, automation, privacy, and the choices that shape everyday digital life.

title: A Little Bit of Code
author: Lena Moss
description: A welcoming path into programming fundamentals using small experiments, plain language, and projects that make the invisible feel tangible.

title: Designing for Humans
author: June Arlen
description: A field guide to accessible, understandable digital products, from first sketch to the small details that help more people belong.

title: The Open Web Handbook
author: Caleb Reed
description: A concise guide to the principles, tools, and practical habits behind a more open, resilient, and user-respecting web.

title: A History of Small Rooms
author: Nadia Hart
description: How kitchens, studies, cells, and rented rooms reveal the changing shape of ordinary life across four centuries.

title: The Making of a City
author: Jon Bell
description: An accessible history of how trade, migration, rivers, and public imagination turn a settlement into a city.

title: Letters from the Archive
author: Amelia Fox
description: A selection of vivid personal letters that puts names, voices, and daily details back into the familiar outline of the past.

title: The Long Nineteenth Century
author: Milo Grant
description: A brisk survey of the inventions, movements, conflicts, and ideas that reshaped the modern world between revolutions.

title: The Life of a Listener
author: Rae Okafor
description: The life and work of a community radio host who spent five decades asking better questions and making room for overlooked voices.

title: Hands That Built a Home
author: Sana Cole
description: A portrait of a builder, teacher, and neighborhood organizer whose patient work changed the shape of a whole block.

title: The Painter of Blue Mornings
author: Faye Linden
description: An intimate account of an artist who turned a difficult childhood, a changing coastline, and a lifelong practice into luminous paintings.

title: A Life in Margins
author: Elian Rose
description: The story of a scholar whose handwritten notes, marginalia, and quiet mentorship influenced generations of readers.

title: The Weeknight Table
author: Mina Sol
description: Forty flexible recipes for busy evenings, built around pantry staples, fresh vegetables, and the pleasure of feeding people well.

title: Bread Without Fuss
author: Nico Avery
description: A friendly introduction to loaves, flatbreads, and doughs that fit into real schedules instead of demanding a whole weekend.

title: The Spice Drawer
author: Priya Sen
description: A visual, practical guide to getting more from everyday spices, with simple blends and recipes for every level of cook.

title: Preserving the Season
author: Amelia Fox
description: A calm guide to pickles, jams, ferments, and pantry projects that help a good season last a little longer.
